rows.why: This scenario is about parsing well-formed input and adding the components together, which is core behaviour, not an open question. Some rows touch other items: '2d' needs days (item 6), and '0s' and the zero parts in '1d0h0m0s0ms' need zero counts (item 10). But no single item's answer settles the whole scenario.
Item 1 asks whether whitespace around the input is accepted. The pick trims it before parsing, so '  45m\n' gives 2700000, as the scenario expects.

This scenario covers many items: empty (3), bare number (4), inner whitespace (2), case (5), unknown unit (6), leading zero (10). Item 8 is the closest because it settles the most rows: '1.5h', '-3s', '+3s' and the full-width '３s'. Its pick of unsigned ASCII digits only rejects all four. Note a conflict on another row: item 10's pick accepts leading zeros ('007s'), so '05s' would parse, but the scenario expects it to be rejected.
No item asks whether a count may be larger than the next unit up, as in '90m' being more than an hour. Item 7 is about unit order and repeats, which is a different question.
Item 7 asks whether units may appear out of order or repeat. The pick requires largest to smallest with each unit at most once, so '30m1h', '1h1h', '1s500ms2s' and '5ms1s' are all rejected.
Item 9 asks for the maximum duration. The pick caps it at 2^53-1 ms (9007199254740991), which counts as valid, so the largest-value string parses to exactly that.
Item 9 also covers what happens past the maximum or on overflow. The pick returns 0 and an error when a count, a product or the sum goes over 2^53-1, which matches both rows.

Item 12 asks whether the formatter breaks a value into several units. The pick splits greedily into d/h/m/s/ms with days largest and leaves out zero parts, which gives '1m30s', '1h30m', '1d' and '1d1h1m1s1ms'. The 0 → '0ms' row is item 11, whose pick also agrees.
2^53-1 is inside the pick's range, and the greedy split with days largest gives '104249991d8h59m991ms'.
No item asks whether formatting then parsing gives the number back. That follows from the formatter and parser agreeing, which isn't one of the open questions.

Item 12 asks how the formatter handles negative or oversized values. The pick returns "" and an error for values below 0 or above 2^53-1, which covers every row. The pick doesn't give the error wording, so whether the message contains 'milliseconds' can't be checked from the list.
